name: persistence_normalise
description: Scheduled tasks, services and autorun keys linked to their registration and execution evidence, without a persistence verdict. Inputs, any of which may be given (at least one hive or tasks_dir): software, the SOFTWARE hive (the TaskCache: Tree, Tasks, Plain, Boot, Logon, Maintenance; and the autorun keys Run and RunOnce, Wow6432Node Run and RunOnce, Winlogon Shell and Userinit, Windows AppInit_DLLs and LoadAppInit_DLLs, Image File Execution Options Debugger, Active Setup StubPath); system, the SYSTEM hive (every ControlSetNNN Services key); ntuser, an NTUSER.DAT (Run and RunOnce of that user); tasks_dir, a directory of Task Scheduler XML files (Windows\System32\Tasks, walked without following links; a pipe, a link or another non-regular entry is counted and never opened; a file over 8 MiB is refused); evtx_results, an evtx_query result file (JSON Lines; there is no import of other tools). Every item has a mechanism: scheduled_task, service or autorun. A scheduled_task item is one per task path, with its registration evidence (xml, tree, tree_sd, tasks_key: present, absent or not_provided; the Plain, Boot, Logon and Maintenance groups), the XML fields with locators (URI, author, date, principal, trigger kinds, each action's kind, command, arguments, working directory; at most 50 actions listed, the rest counted), the TaskCache Actions and Triggers values as bytes (actions_hex, triggers_hex). NOT DONE: the Actions and Triggers structures are not decoded (the package asks for their documented layouts; none could be checked against a real hive, so none is guessed), the XML is the readable definition; a value of either that is not binary data is kept as given (actions_value, triggers_value with their registry type) and listed under unsupported_fields, and DynamicInfo decoded by its length (28 or 36 bytes) and first number (2 or 3) with the layout and its basis (unsupported, bytes kept, when it fits neither). Task XML is decoded by the tool itself and never left to the XML parser to detect: UTF-16 (either order) or UTF-8 by its byte order mark, UTF-16 with no byte order mark by the pattern of its NUL bytes (also after a UTF-8 byte order mark), and text with NUL bytes that is not UTF-16 is refused; a DOCTYPE or ENTITY declaration is looked for in the decoded text and in the bytes with their NULs taken out, and refused before any parse, so no entity is ever expanded; malformed XML is refused with a fixed reason (xml_refused). A service item is one per service per control set: ImagePath, DisplayName and ObjectName as text (a value of another type, such as REG_BINARY, REG_MULTI_SZ or REG_DWORD, is kept as given in image_path_value, display_name_value or object_name_value with its registry type, listed under unsupported_fields, and makes the answer partial), Start and Type as numbers with the documented label (unknown outside them; a value that is not a number is labelled so and makes the answer partial), Parameters ServiceDll (the same for a value that is not text), FailureActions as bytes (not decoded), the key it came from, the control set and whether it is the current one (Select Current). An autorun item is one per value: its kind (run, runonce, winlogon, appinit, ifeo, active_setup), hive, key, value name and the command text; a binary value is kept as bytes and is unsupported. ImagePath, ServiceDll, Run values and Debugger are command lines and can carry secrets: they are withheld by shape and written whole only in a job run as secret output. Observations are facts about the inputs, never verdicts: xml_without_taskcache, taskcache_without_xml, tree_entry_without_sd_value (the shape a hidden task has), tree_entry_without_tasks_key, tasks_key_without_tree_entry, events_only; tasks are only compared when both sides were provided; a service with neither an ImagePath nor a ServiceDll value of any type is stated as no_imagepath_and_no_servicedll_value. Execution evidence is filled only from evtx_results: Security 4698 to 4702 and Microsoft-Windows-TaskScheduler/Operational 106, 140, 141, 200 and 201, matched to a task by the TaskName data field, case-insensitively; at most 200 events are listed per task, the rest are counted (events_not_listed); a line of the result file over 8 MiB is counted and dropped, not read, and a row whose event_id is not a number is ignored. WMI repository: not examined; permanent subscriptions are never read. The offsets of DynamicInfo and the Start and Type labels are those the published notes give and are not verified against a real hive. Second reader: NOT DONE. No RECmd, RegRipper or Dissect reader is started (cross_check is always not_run), so the tool has no child process; nothing in the answer is cross-checked by an independent reader. The hive is read as it is: hives holds, for each hive read, hive_dirty from the base block's sequence numbers and the transaction logs beside the hive are named and not replayed; every list of subkeys and values is read through the size of the hive. Problems are a page (the first 40 inline, all in all_problems); the items are a page (limit inline, the whole result as JSON Lines named in all_results, never replaced by a smaller one). The tool reads until 264 seconds of its own time limit of 294 (a tenth of it is kept for writing) and says partial, naming at least how many entries were not read (the entries of the directory, key or list in hand and the services of later control sets; directories and keys not started are counted apart, what they hold and every source after the stop are not counted, and the answer says so); what was read is then written within the rest of the 294 seconds, and the items read and not written are counted apart. A list of more than 100,000 items, or too long for half the time left, is listed in a random order (the answer says so and is partial) instead of in the order of the text shown; SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP end it with JSON and no temporary file. status is complete only when every file, key and line named was read and decoded: a refused task file, an unsupported DynamicInfo or other value of the wrong type, a problem, events past the listing, a skipped link or pipe, a time stop, a dirty hive and a blind filter each make it partial, and status_basis says which. WITHHOLDING (one boundary on every way out). Every key and value of the answer, and every row of every file this tool writes, is judged by the type of the field it fills (paths, names, publishers and hashes): a name, path, key or URL is shown as it is only when it fits a plain grammar (a path component by component; GUIDs, SIDs, addresses, 0x numbers, times and hexadecimal ids up to 24 digits are plain), free text has token-shaped runs, user-info, the value after a secret's name, vendor-prefixed tokens, padded base64 and PEM keys withheld, and a second check written apart from the first reads it all once more, the text as the evidence wrote it as well as the text shown (a piece of 12 characters of a secret that two cuts left behind is caught) (a string it replaces makes a complete answer partial and is listed under boundary.replaced_at, by the keys on the way as they are shown or by positions, never by a withheld key). ORDER: the items are taken in the order of the text shown for each task path (withheld paths in an order of their own that is new for every run), not the order the hive or the directory stores them. FILTER: `contains` is looked for in the text the answer prints for the task path, the URI, and each action's command and arguments (never in what the boundary withheld); an item not matched whose printed text holds a withheld part is counted (contains_blind_records) and makes the answer partial, because the needle may be in what is withheld; the name of a result file never depends on the filter's text. Command and Arguments of a task can carry secrets: they are withheld by shape like every other text, and the full text is in the values file only in a job run as secret output. A withheld text is <withheld N characters: reason>. Past the judging time (SEAL_BUDGET, 10 seconds for an answer or a row, and never past the seal stop of the tool, which is 3.5 seconds before its time limit because the string being judged at that point is finished first and one string of 256 KiB can take up to 2.3 seconds) the strings the evidence supplied are no longer judged: each is replaced whole by <withheld N bytes: backstop: the judging time ran out>, counted and listed, and the answer is partial, except the names this tool wrote itself (its keys, the names of its result files, the name of the hive, its status basis) and a string of 15 characters or fewer made only of letters, digits, _ and . that does not start like a vendor token and, in a field of a typed kind (a SID, a GUID, a digest), fits the grammar of its type (so not a Slack-shaped token, not the value after a flag such as -pwd, not a prefix and 12 characters). The seal stop ends the judging only, not the tool's own work, which has its own, earlier clock. When any part of a free-text string is withheld, the line breaks, tabs and invisible characters of that string are not kept in the text shown (it is judged without them); a string with nothing withheld is shown exactly as it is. Binary data written as hexadecimal is decoded and judged by its printable text, by both layers and by the backstop on its own; hexadecimal with no secret-shaped text in it is shown as it is, random bytes included (a binary key is printed). write_values: true writes the originals of everything withheld to <tool>-values.jsonl (mode 0600, created first, never replaced) and is accepted only in a job the harness runs as secret output (the manifest declares it; SECRET_OUTPUT=1), refused as JSON anywhere else before anything is made. Measured on random plants of every shape in 13 slots (988 per shape, five independent runs, 4,940 per shape; rates, not guarantees; the tests plant them again): prefixed tokens (GitHub, GitLab, Stripe, SendGrid, Google, npm, AWS key ids), JWT, PEM keys (one line and several), connection strings, user-info (an @, a / or a + inside the password, a random user of any length, a GitLab token glued to hexadecimal digits), NUL, zero-width and full-width splits, upper-case and glued prefixes: 0 printed whole in 4,940 plants of each shape and no piece of 12 characters of one printed; AWS-shaped secret keys of 40 characters: about 0.1% printed whole (0 whole and 1 piece of 12 characters in 4,940 plants of the block's own harness; 1 of 105 canaries end to end, the same canary in four slots; an earlier measurement found 2 whole and 3 pieces in 4,940), so the rate is small and not zero. The shapes that are not zero, as the range of the five runs over all slots with the worst single slot (76 plants, one plant is 1.3%) beside it: 16, 20 and 32-byte base64 keys 0.0% to 0.3% (worst slot 1.3%; up to 3.9% in end-to-end runs); random base62 of 20 to 40 characters 0.0% to 0.3% (worst slot 2.6%); random lower-case letters of 24 9.2% to 10.6% (worst slot 14.5% to 21.1%); a 16-character base32 seed 9.8% to 11.7% (worst slot 15.8% to 21.1%). In a binary slot (a hexadecimal REG_BINARY value or table cell) the backstop decodes the hexadecimal and replaces every hex-encoded shape it claims (480 of 480 plants), but random bytes that hold no text are printed (200 of 200), and so is a hexadecimal secret written as text there (a 32-digit one in a table cell: 97%). Strings changed (any part withheld) on real evidence: in a real 72 MB SOFTWARE hive (3,000 strings sampled per class) 3.7% of key-name components, 1.0% of value names and 0.9% of REG_SZ data (the names of the Windows component store, WinSxS, are not replaced by the backstop in a name, key or path); in real event logs (175 logs, 64,716 records, up to 4 MB each) the XML of 2.0% of the records is replaced whole by the backstop (5.6% before the shape guard of this round; Security 0.1%, was 6.7%), 1.7% of the data fields are withheld (3.7% before, process ids no longer) and 45 of the 175 runs end partial (84 before). The average hides channels: PowerShell/Operational has the XML of 25.0% of its 1,857 records replaced whole (script blocks carry base64 and long identifiers) and CodeIntegrity/Operational 33.3% of its 1,309 (event 3089, whose Hash is a padded base64 digest). Strings the shape rules change that are not secrets: numbers of 19 digits or more (handles, a Chrome field-trial handle, a mojo pipe name), unlabelled hexadecimal runs of 32 digits or more (the native-image directories), and the query values of a URL in a URL slot. NOT recognised, by design: a secret that does not look like one (a plain password or passphrase, a pronounceable passphrase, a UUID-shaped key, a hexadecimal secret of up to 24 digits in a name or of any length in a binary slot, anything under 16 characters in a name; 69% to 100% of such plants are printed): withholding is by shape, so a file whose secrets matter is read in a job run with secret_output: true. DIRTY HIVE: hive_dirty (the two sequence numbers differ), the log files looked for (transaction_logs_looked_for: the hive's name with .LOG1, .LOG2 and .LOG) and the ones beside the hive (transaction_logs_beside_hive) are reported; the logs are NOT replayed, so every answer that read a dirty hive (hives says which of them) is partial and status_basis names the caveat (what is read is the hive file as it is, and keys and values may differ from the live registry; registry_recover replays the logs on a copy, which this tool then reads). A log that is not among the files the job can read is not found: declare the hive's .LOG1 and .LOG2 as inputs of the job. INLINE VALUES: a value whose data is inside its record (four bytes at most) is read from the record for every registry type. regipy 6.3.0 reads up to 2 GiB of the hive file for such a value and returns that for a type it has no branch for (a device property under a Properties key, REG_LINK, REG_FILETIME, an unknown type), so one such value came back as megabytes of the hive; this tool replaces that read. BIG DATA AND REG_MULTI_SZ: the values of a key are read by this tool from regipy's copy of the hive, with regipy 6.3.0's records, names, types and decoding, and a value of more than 16,344 bytes that is kept in segments (a db record) is checked before its data is put together: one that declares more data than the hive file holds past its base block, whose list holds fewer segments than its size needs, runs past the end of the file or names one segment more than once, or one of whose segments lies past the end of the file, is not read; it is named under problems by its place in the key's value list and its type, and the answer is partial (regipy put together whatever the list named: one 16 KB segment named 160 times was a 2.5 MiB value, and a 548 KB hive declared one of 2 GiB). Every value's data counts against the walk's data budget (four times the hive's size) before it is read. A REG_MULTI_SZ is split by this tool in one pass and gives the strings regipy gives (empty ones left out); the bytes after its last NUL, and a string that is not valid UTF-16 with the rest of the data after it, are not in the answer, as with regipy, and are said under problems with their length (regipy dropped them without a word, and took 50 s on 2 MiB with no NUL). The tool's deadline is read before every value and every 256 subkey elements of a list begun before it: the values or subkeys of a key that were not read in time are said under problems.

software.description: Path to the SOFTWARE hive (the TaskCache and the autorun keys)

system.description: Path to the SYSTEM hive (the service keys)

ntuser.description: Path to an NTUSER.DAT (that user's Run and RunOnce keys)

tasks_dir.description: Path to a directory of Task Scheduler XML files (Windows/System32/Tasks of the collection)

evtx_results.description: Path to an evtx_query result file (JSON Lines) holding Security 4698 to 4702 and TaskScheduler/Operational 106, 140, 141, 200, 201

contains.description: Keep items whose printed path, URI, command, arguments or image path contain this text, case-insensitively; looked for only in the text the answer prints

limit.description: Items shown inline (default 500, an inline page size); every item is kept, and when there are more the whole list is written as JSON Lines and named in all_results

write_values.description: Write the originals of everything the boundary withheld to a file under $OUT (mode 0600, created first, never replaced): only in a job run with secret_output: true, refused anywhere else; default false
